## Description

<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:BEGIN -->
LCLI-144 (wave 11) fixed the write/read profile asymmetry for `lore validate` only, by exempting the reserved root docs/index.md via effectiveProfileFor in src/core/validate.ts. The SAME root cause survives at the loadBundle seam: src/core/bundle.ts loadBundle parses every concept via tryParseConcept against the caller-forwarded ACTIVE profile and throws a validation LoreError on failure, so loadBundle-based commands still fail on a freshly scaffolded bundle under a custom profile that adds a required field to the Reference type. Empirically confirmed by the LCLI-144 review: in a scratch project where `lore validate` now passes, `lore graph` exits 6 with "invalid Reference frontmatter in index.md: owner: expected string, received undefined". `lore check` passes clean (separate parse path). IMPORTANT for the fix: loadBundles path space is bundle-root-relative ("index.md"), NOT repo-relative ("docs/index.md"), so a naive reuse of validate.ts effectiveProfileFor would silently miss — the reserved-root exemption must be applied in loadBundle at the bundle-relative root index path. Likely-affected commands share the loadBundle-profile-forwarding pattern (graph confirmed; query/sync/link/context are the same call shape). Wave-11 (LCLI-144) per-task review finding (medium).
<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:END -->

## Acceptance Criteria
<!-- AC:BEGIN -->
- [x] #1 A freshly scaffolded bundle (`lore init`) under an active profile that adds a required field to the Reference type can run loadBundle-based commands (e.g. `lore graph`) without a validation error on the reserved root docs/index.md
- [x] #2 The reserved-root exemption is applied at loadBundles bundle-relative root index path (not a repo-relative match), consistent with LCLI-144s validate.ts carve-out
- [x] #3 A regression test covers init-then-graph (or another loadBundle command) under such a profile, asserting no validation failure on the scaffolded root index; existing behavior for non-root concepts unchanged
<!-- AC:END -->

## Implementation Plan

<!-- SECTION:PLAN:BEGIN -->
1. Generalize the LCLI-144 root-index profile carve-out (currently private effectiveProfileFor in validate.ts, comparing the repo-relative docs/index.md) into a shared, exported helper. 2. Since validate.ts already imports nodeText from bundle.ts, moving the helper into bundle.ts (not the reverse) avoids a circular import; validate.ts imports it back. 3. Generalize the helper's signature to take an explicit rootIndexPath parameter so each caller supplies its own path-space constant: validate.ts keeps its repo-relative ROOT_INDEX_PATH (docs/index.md) from scaffold.ts; bundle.ts adds its own bundle-relative constant (index.md) since loadBundle's walk paths are bundle-root-relative. 4. Wire loadBundle to resolve each concept's effective profile through this helper before calling tryParseConcept, so the scaffolded root index is judged against defaultProfile() while every other concept keeps the caller's active profile. 5. Add a regression test in test/graph.test.ts: init a bundle under a custom profile that requires an extra Reference field, then run graph (loadBundle-based) and assert no validation failure on the root index; assert a non-root Reference concept still fails the required-field check under the same profile.
<!-- SECTION:PLAN:END -->

## Implementation Notes

<!-- SECTION:NOTES:BEGIN -->
Implemented: exported effectiveProfileFor(path, rootIndexPath, profile) from src/core/bundle.ts (generalized from validate.ts's private helper, now taking an explicit rootIndexPath so callers supply their own path-space constant), moved there instead of the reverse to avoid a circular import (validate.ts already imports nodeText from bundle.ts). Added BUNDLE_ROOT_INDEX_PATH = "index.md" (loadBundle's own bundle-relative spelling, distinct from scaffold.ts's repo-relative ROOT_INDEX_PATH = "docs/index.md"). loadBundle now resolves each concept's effective profile via effectiveProfileFor(rel, BUNDLE_ROOT_INDEX_PATH, profile) before calling tryParseConcept. validate.ts now imports and calls the shared effectiveProfileFor(path, ROOT_INDEX_PATH, profile) instead of its own private copy — the two carve-outs share one algorithm and cannot drift apart.

Verification:
- bun test: 1913 pass, 0 fail, 5385 expect() calls (full suite, up from 1911 baseline — 2 new tests added).
- bun run typecheck (tsc --noEmit): clean, no errors.
- bun run lint on changed files (src/core/bundle.ts, src/core/validate.ts, test/graph.test.ts): zero errors/infos on all three; the lint script's residual failures are pre-existing red-baseline in files this task did not touch (managed-block.ts/.test.ts, supersede.test.ts, context.test.ts, replace.test.ts, validate.test.ts's own unrelated import-order line).
- Empirical AC#1 proof: scaffolded a scratch bundle (bun run src/cli.ts init) under a custom .lore/profile.toml requiring Reference.owner. Pre-fix (verified by temporarily reverting bundle.ts+validate.ts via git diff/apply -R, per the no-git-stash rule, then reapplying): `lore graph` exited 6 with "invalid Reference frontmatter in index.md: owner: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined" while `lore validate` passed clean (0 errors) — reproducing the exact LCLI-144/LCLI-192 asymmetry described in the task. Post-fix: `lore graph` exits 0, emitting "1 concept, 0 edges, ~103 tokens ... index [Reference] ~103 Documentation" — no validation error on the scaffolded root index.
- Regression test added in test/graph.test.ts (describe "loadBundle — LCLI-192 reserved root index under a custom profile"): (1) init-then-graph succeeds under the custom profile and the root index node is present as type Reference; (2) a non-root docs/reference/orders.md Reference concept still throws a validation error citing "owner" under the same profile via a direct loadBundle call — proving the exemption is root-index-only.
<!-- SECTION:NOTES:END -->

## Final Summary

<!-- SECTION:FINAL_SUMMARY:BEGIN -->
Fixed the loadBundle-seam sibling of LCLI-144: loadBundle in src/core/bundle.ts now exempts the reserved bundle-root index (bundle-relative "index.md", via a new BUNDLE_ROOT_INDEX_PATH constant) from the caller's active profile, judging it against defaultProfile() instead — matching how scaffold.ts always writes it. The exemption logic (effectiveProfileFor) was generalized and moved from a private function in validate.ts into an exported function in bundle.ts (validate.ts already depends on bundle.ts, so this direction avoids a circular import), taking an explicit rootIndexPath so validate.ts's repo-relative carve-out (docs/index.md) and bundle.ts's bundle-relative one (index.md) share one algorithm without either accidentally matching the other's path space. Verified: bun test 1913/1913 pass (0 fail), bun run typecheck clean, and an empirical scratch-bundle repro — lore init under a custom profile requiring Reference.owner, then lore graph — went from exit 6 (validation error on the scaffolded root index) pre-fix to exit 0 post-fix, while a non-root Reference concept under the same profile still correctly fails. Regression test added in test/graph.test.ts.
<!-- SECTION:FINAL_SUMMARY:END -->
